newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM palladium futures surge by daily limit.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM palladium futures surge by daily limit.

text.p: All yen-based Tokyo palladium futures ended at their daily limits on Thursday, while platinum futures retreated from early highs to end mixed after news that the strike at South Africa's Amplats was over, traders said.
Palladium futures across the board surged by their 24 yen per gram daily limit. Benchmark April was up 24 yen at 613 yen.

"Palladium jumped from the outset following prices soaring to a 17-year high in New York. In the morning, investors who could not buy palladium rushed to buy platinum futures. But as the news of the end of the strike spilled over, investors switched to selling the distant months," one trader said.
Platinum futures ranged from 14 yen per gram lower to 25 yen firmer. Benchmark April platinum ended 13 down at 1,385 yen.
Trade in platinum futures was buoyant, while palladium futures were stuck to the daily limit highs throughout the day.
"Caution that platinum has been overbought, prompted active selling late in the day, but sentiment in palladium appears to be bullish," an analyst at a commodity broker said.

Despite of expectations that Russian PGM sales will resume soon, the extremely tight physical market and heavy short positions held by private investors on TOCOM were raised as bullish factors, traders said.
Gold futures ended narrowly mixed with prices moving in line with the currency market.
Prices ranged from three yen per gram lower to six higher, with benchmark April ending six yen up at 1,288 yen.
Japan's gold imports in April fell by 7.8 percent from a year earlier to 8.64 tonnes, Finance Ministry data showed.
"The increase in sales tax in April dampened that month's gold investment demand," one trader said.
Spot gold was quoted at $345.50/346.00 at 0751 GMT, against 344.60/345.10 in New York on Wednesday. Benchmark April silver was down 1.7 yen per 10 grams at 179.2 yen.
